title: Finite-type calculus and representable compatibility for stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Locally of finite type for stacks is tested on smooth scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with the scheme notion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; finite type means locally of finite type and quasi-compact, where quasi-compact means that for every affine scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ the point space of the base change is quasi-compact; the point space uses field objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with its smooth-atlas topology. Representable by algebraic spaces means that every scheme base change is equivalent to an algebraic space. Properties of such maps are tested on these algebraic-space base changes. For composable morphisms $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $g:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ of Deligne--Mumford stacks, if both are locally of finite type, respectively of finite type, then so is $g\circ f$. These properties are preserved by arbitrary base change between Deligne--Mumford stacks. If $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces, either property holds for $f$ if and only if it holds for every algebraic-space map $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X\to T$, for schemes $T\to\mathcal Y$. In particular on algebraic spaces these stack notions agree with the ordinary notions. For algebraic spaces, locally of finite type is tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and finite type additionally means quasi-compact. More precisely, the smooth chart test for local finite type can be made on a smooth scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$ and a smooth scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$: the scheme map $U\to V$ must be locally of finite type. The condition is independent of the chosen presentation. In the universal compatible-chart formulation, the induced map $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is required to be smooth. For the ordinary algebraic-space notions, a space is quasi-compact when it admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, and a map $E\to F$ is quasi-compact when $E\times_F Z$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic space $Z\to F$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=$ locally of finite type for algebraic-space morphisms. The smooth-locality node supplies exactly conditions (i)--(iii) in the general smooth chart-comparison theorem, and also fppf target locality. Therefore its equivalent conditions (A) and (B), including their scheme-chart forms, apply to $\mathcal P$. In a relative presentation $V\to\mathcal Y$, $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, both chosen as smooth surjective scheme atlases, the composite $U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth surjective by chartwise smooth base change and composition. Thus (A) implies local finite type of $U\to V$, and conversely this one presentation satisfies (B). This makes the smooth scheme-chart convention in the statement precise and proves its independence of presentation. Etale relative presentations exist for all DM stacks and their fibre products by the DM atlas-calculus node, and etale maps are smooth by chartwise calculus. Surjectivity here uses the current chartwise statement: a field-valued target object lifts after a field extension. For representable maps it is equivalent to surjectivity of the scheme map on each surjective etale chart of a scheme pullback; no lift over the original field is required.

Suppose $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $g:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ are locally of finite type. Choose an etale scheme atlas $W\to\mathcal Z$, an etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal Z}W$, and an etale scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. The DM atlas-calculus node ensures existence and says that the resulting $V\to\mathcal Y$ and $U\to\mathcal X$ are etale surjective. In particular these are smooth, and the relative atlas maps are smooth. Condition (A) from step 1 applied to $g$ and $f$ gives local finite type of $V\to W$ and $U\to V$. These are scheme maps, so representable chartwise calculus gives local finite type of $U\to W$. The diagram $U\to W$ above $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z$ has smooth vertical maps and surjective source map, and hence satisfies (B) for $g f$. Thus the composite is locally of finite type. Condition (B) does not require the induced relative map to be smooth.

Let $h:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$ be arbitrary and put $\mathcal X'=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y'$. Choose etale scheme atlases $V\to\mathcal Y$, $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, and $V'\to\mathcal Y'\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. Their composite maps to $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y'$ are etale surjective by DM atlas calculus. Step 1 gives local finite type of $U\to V$. The scheme map $A=U\times_VV'\to V'$ is locally of finite type by arbitrary base change for representable maps in chartwise calculus. The map $A\to\mathcal X'\times_{\mathcal Y'}V'$ is the base change of the atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, so is etale surjective. Consequently $A\to\mathcal X'$ is etale surjective. The diagram $A\to V'$ above $\mathcal X'\to\mathcal Y'$ satisfies condition (B) of chart comparison; the base-changed map is locally of finite type. Nothing here assumes $h$ representable or smooth.

The affine-test definition of quasi-compactness of a DM stack map $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is equivalent to the following condition: for every quasi-compact DM stack $\mathcal T\to\mathcal Y$, the stack $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal T$ is quasi-compact. Indeed choose an affine smooth surjective atlas $A\to\mathcal T$ by the quasi-compact atlas criterion. The affine-test assumption makes $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}A$ quasi-compact. DM atlas calculus makes these fibre products DM, and chartwise base change makes $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}A\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal T$ smooth surjective. Condition (4) of the quasi-compact atlas criterion then makes its target quasi-compact. The converse follows by taking $\mathcal T$ affine.

Suppose $f$ and $g$ are quasi-compact. Given a quasi-compact DM stack and a map $k:\mathcal T\to\mathcal Z$, step 4 first makes $\mathcal Y_{\mathcal T}=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal T$ quasi-compact using $g$, and then makes $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y_{\mathcal T}$ quasi-compact using $f$. Explicitly, over each test scheme its objects are $(x,(y,t,\beta),\alpha)$ with $\alpha:f(x)\simeq y$ and $\beta:g(y)\simeq k(t)$. Send this to $(x,t,\beta\circ g(\alpha))$; the inverse sends $(x,t,\gamma)$ to $(x,(f(x),t,\gamma),\mathrm{id})$. These functors act on arrows componentwise, and $\alpha$ identifies their composite with the identity. Thus this last stack is equivalent to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal T$. Thus $g f$ is quasi-compact by step 4. Together with step 2 and the definition finite type $=$ locally of finite type plus quasi-compact, this proves finite-type composition.

If $f$ is quasi-compact and $h:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$ is arbitrary, write $k:\mathcal T\to\mathcal Y'$ for a map from a quasi-compact DM stack. The iterated fibre product $(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y')\times_{\mathcal Y'}\mathcal T$ is equivalent over $\mathcal T$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal T$. Over any test scheme its objects are $(x,y',t,\alpha,\beta)$ with $\alpha:f(x)\simeq h(y')$ and $\beta:y'\simeq k(t)$ in $\mathcal Y'$. Send this object to $(x,t,h(\beta)\circ\alpha)$; the inverse sends $(x,t,\gamma)$ to $(x,k(t),t,\gamma,\mathrm{id})$. These operations act componentwise on arrows and commute with pullback. The arrow $\beta$ identifies the other composite with the identity. The latter stack is quasi-compact by step 4 applied to $f$ and $h k$. Hence the base change is quasi-compact by step 4, and with step 3 this proves base-change stability of finite type.

Now suppose $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Every algebraic-space map is representable by algebraic spaces: its scheme pullbacks are algebraic spaces by the space fibre-product theorem. Apply the representable part of chartwise calculus to obtain arbitrary algebraic-space base-change stability of $\mathcal P$. The locality node gives fppf target locality. Thus both extra hypotheses of the last assertion of smooth chart comparison hold, and that assertion proves that $f$ is locally of finite type if and only if each algebraic-space projection $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T$ is locally of finite type, for schemes $T\to\mathcal Y$. The algebraic-space clause of the same comparison theorem identifies the chart convention with the ordinary notion when source and target are algebraic spaces.

proof.text: For a representable $f$, write $E_T=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. Ordinary quasi-compactness of an algebraic-space map means that every base change by a quasi-compact algebraic space has quasi-compact source. The space point/atlas criterion identifies quasi-compactness of an algebraic space with quasi-compactness of its point space. Suppose $f$ satisfies its affine stack tests. For a quasi-compact algebraic space $Z\to T$, view $Z$ as a discrete DM stack and apply step 4 to $Z\to T\to\mathcal Y$. It gives quasi-compactness of $|\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}Z|$. The space criterion and $E_T\times_TZ\simeq\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}Z$ show that $E_T\to T$ is ordinarily quasi-compact. Conversely, if every $E_T\to T$ is ordinarily quasi-compact, take $T$ affine and the quasi-compact space $Z=T$ to obtain the affine stack tests. Thus quasi-compactness agrees under representable tests. For a map between algebraic spaces, ordinary quasi-compactness gives its affine stack tests immediately, while step 4 gives all ordinary quasi-compact space tests from those affine tests. Combine these equivalences with step 7 to obtain finite-type representable compatibility and agreement of both ordinary notions with the stack notions.

tool_uses.why: Generic existence of algebraic-space fibre products verifies that algebraic-space maps are representable by spaces; the unit has no replacement construction.

Only its last sentence, quasi-compact point space iff quasi-compact etale scheme presentation, identifies the ordinary algebraic-space notion. This is a generic topology tool, not a replacement for the unit route.
